---

Studying advanced string algorithms requires a fundamentally different training protocol from learning introductory string templates. Copying a Suffix Automaton or Palindromic Tree from your library takes two minutes; recognizing *why* a contest problem collapses via the **Weak Periodicity Lemma**, **Significant Suffixes**, **Bannai's Lyndon-Root Runs**, **$[l+L-1, r]$-Clipped $\text{endpos}$ Merging**, or **Tiskin's Unit-Monge Seaweed Permutation** is what separates grandmasters from template users.

This page provides four targeted **Multi-Track Study Roadmaps (`Tracks A–D`)**, the complete **30-Chapter Zero-Forward-Reference Prerequisite DAG**, the **4-Tier Smooth Difficulty Ladder & Blind Checkpoint Protocol (`CP-I`–`CP-VII`)**, and the **Complete 30-Chapter + 7-Checkpoint Mastery Gate Table**. Keep **[Notation, Operators & Failure Modes](notation.qmd)** open alongside your work.

---

## 3. How to Use the 4-Tier Difficulty Ladders & Blind Checkpoints (`CP-I`–`CP-VII`)

### 3.1 The Per-Chapter 4-Tier Smooth Difficulty Ladder (`8`–`10` Problems per Chapter)

Every chapter concludes with a curated problem ladder structured into four deliberate tiers:

1. **Tier 1 · Stepping Stone (`2 Problems`)**: Isolates the core combinatorial word invariant on a clean geometry (e.g., direct `slink` partition count or single-query $[l+L-1, r]$-clipped $\text{endpos}$ lookup). *Goal*: Verify your index boundaries and invariant invariants before adding auxiliary data structures.
2. **Tier 2 · Intermediate (`2 Problems`)**: Couples the chapter's word invariant with a non-trivial bijection or secondary reduction (e.g., double-end interleaving $T = S[1]S[N]S[2]S[N-1]\dots$ in `CF 932G`, or single-witness chain testing in `CF 700E`).
3. **Tier 3 · Advanced (`2`–`3 Problems`)**: Full NOI / Codeforces Div. 1 D–E / AtCoder `ARC`/`AGC` scale problems requiring careful complexity balancing, two-threshold sweeps, or predecessor length jumps (`[NOI2018] 你的名字`, `[ZJOI2017] 字符串`, `[BJWC2018] Border 的四种求法`).
4. **Tier 4 · Mastery (`2 Problems`)**: Grandmaster frontier tasks requiring binomial moment splitting, persistent tree-branching, Unit-Monge $\boxdot$ divide-and-conquer, or $N \le 10^{18}$ compressed/morphic queries (`Universal Cup`, `QOJ`, `国家集训队论文`).

### 3.2 The Unspoiled Blind Checkpoint Protocol & Diagnostic Decoy Pairs

In a real contest, no problem comes labeled *"Use Significant Suffixes (`Ch 06`)"* or *"Use PAM `slink` Telescoping (`Ch 17`)"*. Even worse, many advanced string problems exhibit **nearly identical surface symptoms** while requiring completely different mathematical invariants.

Therefore, each Part concludes with a **Blind Topic-Group Checkpoint (`CP-I`–`CP-VII`)** built around **Diagnostic Decoy Pairs**:

::: {.callout-warning}
## Strict 3-Stage No-Spoiler Protocol for Blind Checkpoints (`CP-I`–`CP-VII`)

When attempting any problem in `CP-I` through `CP-VII`:

1. **Stage 1 · Cold Diagnostic Classification (10–15 Minutes, Zero Hints Open)**:
   - Read the raw mathematical problem statement and constraints ($N, Q, |\Sigma|$, online vs. offline).
   - Without opening any dropdown, write down: (a) why the naive automaton/array approach takes $\Omega(N^2)$, (b) which **Diagnostic Decoy Pair** the problem belongs to, and (c) your candidate combinatorial word invariant.
2. **Stage 2 · Progressive Hint Escalation (`Hint 1` $\to$ `Hint 2` $\to$ `Hint 3`)**:
   - Open **Hint 1 (Diagnostic Signal)** *only* to verify whether you diagnosed the right structural bottleneck—Hint 1 still withholds the exact formula.
   - Open **Hint 2 (Combinatorial Word Invariant)** if you need the double-overlap / periodicity / Monge identity.
   - Open **Hint 3 (Algorithmic Assembly)** if you need the data-structure coupling or boundary clipping rule.
3. **Stage 3 · Post-Solve Counterexample Audit**:
   - After coding or deriving your solution, open the **Complete Derivation & Solution** and check the **Boundary Pitfall** box to ensure your solution survives Sturmian/Fibonacci and prefix-tie counterexamples. Do not advance to the next Part until you solve at least **6 of 7** (or **6 of 8**) blind problems.
:::

### 3.3 The 7-Part Diagnostic Decoy Atlas (Disambiguating Look-Alike Contest Symptoms)

Each blind checkpoint tests whether you can separate competing techniques whose problem statements look nearly identical at first glance:

| Blind Checkpoint | Competing Look-Alike Symptoms (The Decoy Pair / Triad) | Decisive Structural Discriminator |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **[CP-I](checkpoints/cp01-part1-periodicity-borders-slink.qmd)** (`Part I`) | **Online Border Weight Maintenance (`CF 1286E`) vs. Palindrome/Border Partition DP (`CF 932G`)** | If weights change dynamically across all active borders of $S[1..r]$, use **`slink` active-set deletion (`Ch 02`)**; if each left endpoint $i = r - L$ has a fixed prefix DP value $dp[i]$, use **shift-overlap `g[u]` accumulation (`Ch 04`)**. |
| **[CP-II](checkpoints/cp02-part2-lyndon-candidates-runs.qmd)** (`Part II`) | **All-Prefix Minimum Suffix (`Luogu P6127`) vs. Substring Minimum Suffix under Right-Extension (`[ZJOI2017]`)** | When right-extension $T = \varepsilon$ on prefixes $S[1..r]$, **Duval state sharing $r \to r-dp$ (`Ch 05`)** works in $O(1)$; when $T \ne \varepsilon$ or $[l, r]$ is a substring, left-truncation revives killed suffixes (`aaba`), requiring **Significant Suffixes $|\text{Cand}| \le \lfloor \log_2 |U| \rfloor + 1$ (`Ch 06`)**. |
| **[CP-III](checkpoints/cp03-part3-suffix-structures-dominant-pairs.qmd)** (`Part III`) | **External Pattern in $S[l..r]$ (`[NOI2018]`) vs. Internal Pairwise LCP in $S[l..r]$ (`CF 1043G`) vs. Online `push_front` (`[BZOJ 3682]`)** | External pattern containment $\implies$ **$[l+L-1, r]$-clipped $\text{endpos}$ SegTree Merge (`Ch 10`)**; internal $\binom{r-l+1}{2}$ suffix pairs $\implies$ **$2N\log_2 N$ Dominant Pairs (`Ch 13`)**; online encrypted prepend $\implies$ **64-bit Scapegoat Suffix Balanced Tree (`Ch 14`)**. |
| **[CP-IV](checkpoints/cp04-part4-ipm-deque-range-palindromes.qmd)** (`Part IV`) | **Range Longest Border (`[BJWC2018]`) vs. Range Longest Palindrome (`Range LPS`)** | Borders are **non-hereditary** (must intersect dyadic prefix $P_m$ and suffix $Q_m$ APs in $O(\log N)$, `Ch 15`); palindromes are **center-hereditary** (all centers $c \in (c_L, c_R)$ are 100% unclipped, giving **true $O(1)$ Range LPS**, `Ch 17`). |
| **[CP-V](checkpoints/cp05-part5-fft-isomorphism-slp-indexing.qmd)** (`Part V`) | **Involution Matching $\pi^2=\text{id}$ (`CF 1334G`) vs. General $\pi$ vs. Parameterized/Cartesian KMP** | If $\pi^2 = \text{id}$, canonical 2-cycle representatives solve it in **$O(N)$ KMP (`Ch 18`)**; general non-involution $\pi$ requires **FFT (`Ch 18`)**; dynamic bijective renaming or heap shape requires **$O(1)$ window-clipped backward offsets (`Ch 20`)**. |
| **[CP-VI](checkpoints/cp06-part6-subsequences-seaweed-string-gfs.qmd)** (`Part VI`) | **Range Distinct Subsequences vs. Gap-2 / Tropical $(\min,+)$ Subsequences vs. Interval LCS (`[THUPC 2021]`)** | Ring subsequence DP has $\det M_c = 1$ (**$O(|\Sigma|)$ matrix-free dot product $\mathbf{u}_r^T\cdot \mathbf{v}_{l-1}$, `Ch 22`**); gap-2 ($\det=0$) and tropical $(\min,+)$ lack inverses (require Segment Trees); 2-string interval alignment uses **Tiskin's Seaweed $W[k] < l$ (`Ch 23`)**. |
| **[CP-VII](checkpoints/cp07-part7-equations-trees-groups-morphic.qmd)** (`Part VII`) | **Bulk Palindrome Equations (`[SCOI2016]`) vs. Adjacency Stack Cancellation (`CF 1223F`)** | Static substring/palindrome equalities $S[l_1..r_1] = S[l_2..r_2]^R$ use **Signed Binary-Lifting DSU with `is_pal[k][r]` (`Ch 26`)**; dynamic adjacent cancellation `cc` $\to \varepsilon$ uses **Stack-Trie Path $\text{LCA}$ LCE or $GL_2/SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ (`Ch 29`)**. |

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **[Ch 01 · Fine–Wilf & Orbits](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)** | Assumed `KMP`/`Z` | Simultaneous periods $p, q$ above vs. below $p+q-\gcd(p,q)$ | Prove Fine–Wilf via return map $\psi(x)$, derive $|\Sigma|^{p+q-N}$ below threshold, and construct length-$11$ `abaababaaba` for $(5, 8)$. |
| **[Ch 02 · Border APs & Shortcut Links](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd)** | `Ch 01` | Online short append (`CF 1721E`) vs. monotone active-border deletion (`CF 1286E`) | Prove $\pi[u] < \frac{2}{3}u$ and $\pi[\pi[u]] < \frac{1}{2}u$; explain why `anc[u]` coarsens `slink[u]` and enforce half-open $(\text{slink}[u], u]$. |
| **[Ch 03 · Border Modulo Shortest Path](chapters/ch03-border-modulo-shortest-path.qmd)** | `Ch 01, 02` | Reachable overlap lengths $\le W$ ($10^{18}$) vs. static period orbits | Execute modulus switch $m_{\text{old}} \to x_k$ from cycle argmin $u_{\min}$ and relax residue-cycle deques in unbounded order (`[WC2016]`). |
| **[Ch 04 · Series-Link (`slink`) DP](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd)** | `Ch 02` | Palindrome/border partition DP (`CF 932G`, `CF 906E`, polynomial $L^m$) | Prove $\mathcal{I}(u,r) = \mathcal{I}(\text{fail}[u], r-d) \sqcup \{r-\text{len}[\text{slink}[u]]-d\}$, update `g[u]` at odd $r$, and split $(r-i)^m$ binomially. |
| **[CP-I · Blind Gate I](checkpoints/cp01-part1-periodicity-borders-slink.qmd)** | `Ch 01–04` | **Decoy**: Active-border deletion (`Ch 02`) vs. shift-overlap `g[u]` DP (`Ch 04`) | Solve $\ge 6/7$ blind problems without opening Hint 2. |
| **[Ch 05 · CFL, Duval & Necklaces](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)** | `Ch 01` | All-prefix CFL state sharing ($T=\varepsilon$) vs. RLE Duval ($N \le 10^{18}$) & `BBWT` | Prove Duval's $< 2N$ potential $\Phi = 2i+k$, implement $O(1)$ $r \to r-dp$ sharing (`Luogu P6127`), and invert multi-cycle `BBWT`. |

## 5. The 3-Axis Contest Diagnostic Protocol & Postmortem Template

Whenever you face an unfamiliar string task under contest timing, run through three diagnostic axes before writing code:

### Axis 1 · String Scale, Alphabet Size & Compression Regime

| Constraint Regime | Primary Structural & Algorithmic Families |
| :--- | :--- |
| $|S| \le 20,\; N \le 10^4 \text{–} 10^{18}$ | **Automaton DP / `DP套DP` (`Ch 25`)**: Compress inner LCS/Edit/Palindrome DP into a minimal DFA (using `Ch 23`'s 4-instruction Allison–Dix borrow mask for LCS) and run outer DP or matrix exponentiation. |
| $N, Q \le 10^5 \text{–} 5 \times 10^5,\; |\Sigma| \le 26$ | **Log-Sparsity & Data-Structure Couplings (`Parts I–IV`)**: Border/Palindrome `slink` APs (`Ch 02, 04`), Significant Suffixes (`Ch 06`), Runs + 2D sweep (`Ch 08`), SAM + Clipped `endpos` Merge (`Ch 10`), LCT `access` (`Ch 11`), Dominant Pairs (`Ch 13`), Dyadic IPM (`Ch 15`), Deque/Range PAM (`Ch 16, 17`), or $O(|\Sigma|)$ Invertible Subsequence Matrices (`Ch 22`). |
| $N, M \le 5 \times 10^5$ with Non-Transitive Match | **Algebraic/FFT & Structural KMP (`Part V`)**: 1-NTT Degree-Reduced Indicator Wildcards / Kalai / Involutions (`Ch 18`), $O(N\sqrt{k\log k})$ $2k$-Period $k$-Mismatch (`Ch 19`), or Window-Clipped `p-KMP` / `Cartesian-KMP` (`Ch 20`). |
| $|S| \le 5\,000,\; |T|, Q \le 10^5$ (Alignment) | **Bit-Parallel & Unit-Monge Seaweed Algebra (`Ch 23`)**: $O(MN/w)$ Allison–Dix / Myers bitvectors, or Tiskin's Seaweed permutation $W[1..N]$ answering all interval $\text{LCS}(A, B[l..r])$ queries in $O(\log N)$. |
| $N \le 10^{18}$ (Huge / Compressed / Morphic) | **Grammar, Cluster GF & Morphic Engines (`Parts V–VII`)**: Locally Consistent Parsing / Jeż Recompression SLPs & LZ77 2D grids (`Ch 21`), Goulden–Jackson $t = 1 + u$ Moment Shift (`Ch 24`), Euclidean Period Folding (`Ch 26`), $O(1)$ RLBWT Move Structure (`Ch 28`), or Singular Words / 3-Regime $\varphi^k(S_0)$ (`Ch 30`). |

### Axis 2 · Mandatory Pre-Coding Counterexample Sanity Check

Before submitting any advanced string solution, verify these five invariant guards against **[Notation & Failure Modes](notation.qmd)**:

1. **Half-Open Progression Guard**: Did you treat every `slink` chain as half-open $(\text{slink}[u], u]$ with shortest length $\text{len}[\text{slink}[u]] + \text{diff}[u]$, and initialize `g[u] = dp[r - len[slink[u]] - diff[u]]` (`Ch 02, 04`)?
2. **Substring Left-Boundary Clipping Guard**: Did you clip SAM $\text{endpos}_S(u)$ queries to $[l + L - 1, r]$ instead of $[l, r]$, and shrink $L$ to $e_{\max} - l + 1$ before following `link[u]` (`Ch 10`)?
3. **Generalized SAM & Tree Clone Guard**: Did you use 3-case `extend_gsam` in **Trie-BFS order** (avoiding $\Theta(V^2)$ Trie-DFS and $0$-length clones, `Ch 09`), and flush LCT lazy tags via `access(q); splay(q);` before splitting `clone` (`Ch 11`)?
4. **Reversed-Order Prefix-Tie Guard**: When building $>-$Lyndon arrays for Runs (`Ch 07, 08`), did you invert characters $\overline{S}[t] = |\Sigma|+1-S[t]$ keeping sentinel $0 = -\infty$ rather than negating $-\text{rk}_<$ (which fails on $S = \texttt{bab}$)?
5. **Signed DSU & Stack-Hash Depth Guard**: Did you update `is_pal[k][rx] = 1` when `rx == ry` with `rel == 1` in Signed Parallel DSU (`Ch 26`), and index directed Dyck $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ generators by height $(c, \text{bal}[i])$ so `(( )( ))` cannot cancel across depths (`Ch 29`)?

### Problem Postmortem Log Template

```text
Problem / Judge ID / Time before Hint 1:
Contest Symptom vs. Decoy Eliminated:
Core Combinatorial Word Invariant (1-line equality):
Data-Structure / Algebraic Compilation & Complexity:
Counterexample Tested (e.g., abaababaaba, aaba, bab, (( )( ))):
Re-solve Schedule (+14d, +45d):
```
